_README: register-skills.js (19.5k lines) has many hand-rolled copies of idioms that already have canonical helpers elsewhere in the engine: reading game.user.targets directly instead of the target-reader primitive, re-deriving a caster's token instead of calling edhaCasterToken, folding a Roll formula by hand instead of edhaRollFormula, binding chat-card buttons with a raw renderChatMessageHTML hook instead of the button-binder table, emitting the GM-relay socket action by hand instead of edhaSetEdhaFlag/edhaSpendResource, reading/writing the once-per-scene ledger by its raw flag keys instead of the oncePerScene gate/stamp pair, hand-rolling the GM-whisper recipient list instead of edhaGmIds, re-deriving the primary-GM gate instead of edhaDefBuffGmGate, and writing system.resources.<id>.value/max update paths by hand instead of edhaSpendResource/edhaConsumeCost.

An upcoming hygiene pass will consolidate these onto their canonical helpers. This file freezes TODAY'S measured counts so scripts/lint-refs.js pass 20 can enforce a RATCHET the same way pass 7 does for name-keyed dispatch:
- actual occurrences > counts.<key>  -> ERROR (the count may not grow; use the canonical helper instead of hand-rolling the idiom again)
- actual occurrences < counts.<key>  -> ERROR (lower counts.<key> so the ratchet reflects reality — do not let it become fiction)

The regexes that measure each idiom live in scripts/lint-refs.js pass 20, not here. An entry whose count reaches 0 STAYS in this file as a tombstone — it still gates regrowth even after full migration (see name-keyed-allowlist.json's empty-but-present talents list for the same pattern).
DO NOT bump a count to make the gate pass. A grown count is the violation the gate exists to catch; migrate the site onto its canonical helper instead.

resourceWrite REACHED 0 (item 13, 2026-09-06) — and NONE of the last twelve was a spend. Every cost deduction in the engine already went through edhaSpendResource/edhaConsumeCost; the survivors were gains, heals, restores, a lifesteal, a revive-to-1, a Colossus max-HP override and one open-ruling drain, each with its own clamp, relay-on-failure or multi-path update, which is why none of them could simply call a clamped spend/gain. They now go through edhaResourceWrite(actor, resource, changes, options) — the writer that OWNS the path and takes the classification (edhaBookkeepingTag / edhaSpendTag / the site's existing options where the ruling is open) as an argument. Note the measurement's shape: this regex counts a QUOTED literal key, and every canonical writer builds its path from a variable, so 0 is genuinely reachable here where userTargets floors at 1. A count of 1 means someone hand-rolled a literal resource path again; migrate it onto edhaResourceWrite, do not raise the count.

primaryGmGate FLOORS AT 1, and reached it (item 12, 2026-09-06): 20 -> 1. Nineteen hand-derived copies migrated; the ONE survivor is the canonical helper's own body, the same shape userTargets has. The migration found the idiom was serving TWO polarities, which is why a single helper had never absorbed it: sixteen sites wanted the whole gate (isGM AND no other GM has claimed it) and were byte-equivalent to edhaDefBuffGmGate(); three RegionBehavior._handleRegionEvent sites (Civ fortified foundation, dangerous terrain, Fate snare) checked only the second half, deliberately - a region trap must still fire on a player's OWN client in a GM-less session, and adding the isGM half there would silence it (a live-behaviour change and a ruling, not hygiene). So the gate is now DECOMPOSED: edhaNoOtherActiveGM() is the primitive that carries the one remaining occurrence, and edhaDefBuffGmGate() is defined as isGM && edhaNoOtherActiveGM(). A count of 2 means someone hand-rolled the check again; call one of the two helpers, do not raise the count.

userTargets FLOORS AT 1, not 0 (item 14, 2026-09-06). The idiom's canonical helper is a reader — edhaUserTargetTokens() — and a reader cannot read through itself, so its own one-line body is the last remaining occurrence and is the point of the migration rather than a violation of it. All nine call sites (the single-target preUseItem gate, edhaSetUserTargets' clear-all branch, edhaEffectTargets' "prompt" branch, edhaSovTargets, edhaFindMarkGrant, edhaRedirectClick, the pre-use range guard, the adv-attack to:"targets" fan-out, and the next-test-mod multi-target fan-out) now call it. A count of 2 means someone hand-rolled the read again; migrate it, do not raise the count.

dispoFailOpen was ADDED 2026-08-10 (hygiene campaign wave 6), separately from the eight keys above: those eight were all measured on the SAME day this file was first frozen, but dispoFailOpen's originalCount below is wave 6's own landing measurement, not a retroactive part of that first freeze. It tracks the disposition-default fail-open idiom pass 5.2 (R-63) fixed in the shared helpers plus 16 named sites, leaving an explicit ~74-site backlog — this entry ratchets that backlog so it can only shrink from here, the same way the other eight ratchet theirs.
